name: Anterior Insula as Salience Hub for Physical and Social Pain
description: Cross-framework template demonstrating shared neural substrate for physical pain and social distress. Anterior insula serves as integration hub for both bodily and social threat signals.

key_references.citation: Singer, T., et al. (2004). Empathy for pain involves the affective but not sensory components of pain. Science, 303(5661), 1157-1162.
Eisenberger, N. I., Lieberman, M. D., & Williams, K. D. (2003). Does rejection hurt? An fMRI study of social exclusion. Science, 302(5643), 290-292.
Craig, A. D. (2009). How do you feel—now? The anterior insula and human awareness. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 10(1), 59-70.

causal_links.mechanism_summary: Physical pain OR social exclusion signals both activate anterior insula via distinct input pathways
Insula generates unified negative affect signal regardless of pain source (physical/social)
Shared affect pathway explains why social isolation mimics physical pain in behavioral avoidance

### Template SC3: The Architectural Promenade as Multi-Modal PE Orchestration

```yaml
template_id: "ARCH_PROMENADE_PE_ORCHESTRATION_001"
display_id: "SC3"
name: "Architectural Promenade — Temporal Composition of Multi-Modal Prediction Error"

structural_pattern: >
  The architectural promenade is the deliberate design of spatial
  sequence to produce a specific emotional trajectory over time. As
  the visitor moves through the building, they encounter a series of
  THRESHOLDS — transitions between spatial zones that differ in
  spatial volume, light, material, acoustics, temperature, and view.
  Each threshold is a multi-modal PE event: the prediction set formed
  in the preceding zone is tested against the reality of the new zone,
  and the mismatch across all modalities simultaneously produces an
  integrated emotional response.
  
  The sequence of thresholds is the temporal structure of the
  experience — the "score" that the architect composes. Key
  compositional techniques include:
  
  COMPRESSION-RELEASE: A narrow, low, dark, acoustically damped
  space (compression) → a tall, wide, bright, reverberant space
  (release). The compression builds a strong prediction of
  constriction; the release violates it maximally. The emotional
  intensity of the release is proportional to the compression.
  
  GRADUAL REVELATION: A curved path or ascending ramp that
  progressively reveals a space, changing the isovist incrementally
  rather than suddenly. PE is distributed over time rather than
  concentrated at a single threshold.
  
  SPATIAL RHYTHM: Alternation of spatial types (open-closed-open,
  bright-dark-bright, high-low-high) at regular or irregular
  intervals, creating a temporal pattern that engages rhythmic
  prediction (analogous to musical rhythm, M8).
  
  CLIMACTIC REVELATION: A sequence of escalating PE events building
  to a maximum — the Bernini approach to St. Peter's (compressed
  colonnaded approach → expanding piazza → facade revelation →
  entry through narrow doors → explosive interior volume), where
  each transition intensifies the prediction, and the final space
  exceeds all accumulated expectations, producing awe (AX3).
  
  The emotional trajectory depends on both the MAGNITUDE of PE at
  each threshold and the RATE at which thresholds are encountered.
  Too many rapid thresholds → fatigue, overstimulation. Too few
  thresholds over a long path → boredom, disengagement. The
  optimal density of thresholds along the movement path is a
  temporal Goldilocks zone, analogous to L5's optimal rate of
  light change.

higher_order_principle: >
  The architecture-as-composition thesis formalized. As music
  orchestrates auditory PE over time for emotional effect (M12
  BRECVEMA model, musical expectancy mechanisms), architecture
  orchestrates multi-modal PE over space-time. The visitor's
  movement through the building IS the temporal dimension: spatial
  sequence becomes temporal sequence because the body moves
  through space in time. The architect is a composer whose
  medium is the prediction-error trajectory through a spatial
  sequence. This thesis integrates the entire template library:
  L1 (light at transitions), MAT1/MAT3 (material at transitions),
  AX1/AX2/AX4 (acoustic at transitions), MAT2 (thermal at
  transitions), SC1 (navigational predictions along the path),
  SC2 (isovist dynamics along the path), T2 (complexity at
  each point), AX3 (awe at the climax), AX6 (multi-modal
  integration at each threshold).
